+### 2026-10-21 — F14 texture input experiments deferred after production measurements
+
+Owner: implementation engineer; estimate: measured investigation within the unchanged complete roadmap. The intervening commit request confirmed a clean1ceb9b2 worktree. This continuation finishes three isolated experiments against that committed engine. None is adopted: skipping zero/full-mask mixing, retaining both opacity and non-opaque bounds, or retaining only fully opaque regions. The existing renderer and all public model/command/history/source/isolation contracts remain unchanged.
+
+An intrusive developer diagnostic finds105 mixing calls during the large filter-mask gesture;84 have uniformly zero alpha, covering2,882,880pixels. The endpoint prototype eliminates those84 worker calls, leaving21 mixed calls. Awaited mixing time falls141.0→21.0ms in that diagnostic, including transport/scheduling; this is not kernel compute or clean input latency. Its three-pair production study instead observes large filter-mask median per-run p9537.6→39.0ms and near-large29.9→35.2ms. Fewer RPCs do not prove a faster interaction.
+
+Retaining both lower opacity bounds and conservative non-opaque boxes preserves exact pixels but increases pencil-mask median p95:2048-pixel30.6→38.8ms,1800-pixel31.4→39.8ms and900-pixel31.9→40.1ms. Keeping only fully opaque regions restores recalculation of partial bounds. Its large filter-mask median32.9→32.6ms is inconclusive; small filter-mask20.9→27.1ms and individual large inputs up to81.6ms prevent a consistent improvement claim. These are separate contemporaneous-control studies; their baseline timings must not be pooled. The remaining tile/RPC scheduling and mask preparation need further investigation.
+

Independent decoding verifies648 complete source-sized PNGs and648 checksummed projects: all appearances are byte-exact between each prototype and its control; every gesture retains all21 authored x/y/pressure points, one intended operation, original texture bytes and exact model/pixel undo. No overlapping gesture long task is observed, which does not establish the33ms input target. Engine/WASM and all release identities stay unchanged within each study; no competing builds/tests or application edits run during measurement.
+
+The endpoint prototype passes12 focused actual-WASM unit checks,28 native browser cases and its build. The both-bounds variant passes25 of26 initial native checks; its new test incorrectly counts the existing one-pixel CPU allocation probe as coverage readback. A captured stack identifies createCanvas. The corrected check requires exactly that one probe pixel, retains all cold-render pixel assertions and passes. Opaque-only passes its build and all seven targeted cold/partial/cancellation/source-invalidation checks. These remain prototype checks, not claims of new main release functionality or complete production-suite verification.
